title: [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois..., pages 650 bis à 787, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from this and the neighbouring pages). U_1 = U_{0,3} = P^1_Q - {0,1,oo}, with the tangential base point J. U_n is the affine Fermat curve of degree n minus its cusps. It is the abelian cover of U_1 with deck group mu_n^{0,1,oo}/mu_n, which is (Z/n)^2 as a group.

Grothendieck works in the 'abelian approximation' of the arithmetic fundamental group.
- M = Z^{0,1,oo}/Z (diagonal) is H_1(U_1(C), Z), and M_hat = Z_hat(1) (x) M is the abelianized geometric fundamental group.
- E_1 is an extension of Gamma_Q x S_3 by M_hat, split by J; S_3 permutes {0,1,oo}.
- E_n, the subgroup of E_1 lying over nM_hat = M_hat[n], is the corresponding extension for U_n. Its quotient E'_n is Gamma_Q . nM_hat.

A rational point x_n in U_n(Q) gives a section of E'_n, well defined up to nM_hat-conjugacy.

Step 1. Pushing along nM_hat -> M_hat, the section class gives the section class of the image point x_1 in U_1(Q) = Q - {0,1}. This class is the Kummer class of (x, 1-x) in (Q^*)^ (x) M. The map Q^* -> (Q^*)^ is injective, so the class determines x_1.

Step 2. Hence x_n is determined up to the deck transformations defined over Q. These form gamma_n = mu_n(Q)^{0,1,oo}/mu_n(Q), which equals the Q-points of mu_n^3/mu_n (the boundary map to H^1 is injective because Q^*/Q^*n embeds diagonally).

Step 3 (formula 378). For n odd, mu_n(Q) = 1, so gamma_n = 1. Therefore x_n is completely determined by its section class up to M_hat[n]-conjugation. In other words, the abelian section map is injective on U_n(Q).

Step 4. Grothendieck then proposes to list all conjugacy classes of sections and to ask which could 'reasonably' come from rational points. The classes are
H^1(Gamma_Q, nM_hat) ≅ H^1(Gamma_Q, M_hat) ≅ H^1(Gamma_Q, Z_hat(1)) (x) M ≅ (Q^*)^ (x) M ≅ G(Q)^,
where G = G_m^{0,1,oo}/G_m is a 2-dimensional split torus containing the Fermat curves (formula 379).

Next page. The conclusion is that this approximation only sees rational points of the torus G and is blind to the Fermat equation. It is 'typically abelian' and far too coarse, so finer (non-abelian) approximations are needed.

Purpose: testing whether a section-conjecture style description of rational points on the Fermat curves (i.e. Fermat's Last Theorem) could be reached through successive solvable or nilpotent quotients of pi_1 of U_{0,3} and its Fermat covers.
errors: No real error. One small gap: the identification H^1(Gamma_Q, nM_hat) ≅ H^1(Gamma_Q, M_hat) uses multiplication by n. Under this identification the map induced by the inclusion nM_hat ⊂ M_hat becomes multiplication by n, which is injective because (Q^*)^ (x) M is torsion-free. So Step 1 holds, but the two isomorphisms should not be conflated with the restriction map.
For n even, gamma_n = (Z/2)^2. So the injectivity statement in (378) genuinely fails there, as Grothendieck implicitly notes by restricting to odd n.

ideas.what: Using pi_1 sections of the Fermat covers of P^1-{0,1,oo} to locate rational points of Fermat curves, i.e. an anabelian approach to FLT, analysed level by level in a tower of approximations of pi_1
ideas.modern_name: Section conjecture applied to Fermat curves; nilpotent/solvable descent (Ellenberg's 2-nilpotent obstruction; Kim's non-abelian Chabauty philosophy)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (section conjecture, letter to Faltings 1983); Ellenberg (~2000) for nilpotent obstructions; Kim (2005) for unipotent approximations
ideas.where_published: Section conjecture in the Letter to Faltings (1983); the Fermat-specific analysis does not appear there as far as I know

ideas.what: The abelian section class of a point of U_{0,3} is its Kummer class (x, 1-x) in (Q^*)^ (x) M, and this is injective; the fibre ambiguity for U_n is (mu_n^3/mu_n)(Q), which is trivial for n odd
ideas.modern_name: Kummer map / abelian section map for P^1 minus 3 points and its covers

ideas.what: The abelian approximation only detects rational points of the ambient torus G = G_m^3/G_m (the generalized Jacobian), not of the curve, so finer non-abelian quotients are necessary
ideas.modern_name: Abelian level = generalized Jacobian / torus Kummer map; motivation for higher nilpotent levels
ideas.usually_credited_to: Kim, Ellenberg and others (standard motivation in the 2000s)

missed.claim: Grothendieck explicitly ran the section-conjecture programme on the Fermat tower over U_{0,3}. He observed that at the abelian level the section map is injective for odd n, but the space of sections is just G(Q)^ for the torus G, so the method is blind to the Fermat equation, and he called for finer non-abelian approximations. This prefigures Ellenberg's nilpotent obstructions for Fermat curves and Kim's unipotent hierarchy. The explicit Fermat-specific diagnosis by Grothendieck does not seem to be documented in the literature.
missed.quote: Ces classes correspondent aux éléments de H^1(Γ_Q, nM̂) ≃ ... ≃ G(Q)^
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is a historical precedent for Kim-style and Ellenberg-style descent on Fermat curves. It shows Grothendieck tied anabelian geometry, Galois actions on pi_1 of P^1 minus 3 points, and FLT together, at least as an exploratory test.

deep.surprise_reason: The page itself is a routine Kummer-theory computation, and the conclusion that abelian information only gives the torus is standard today. Of interest is mainly the documentation that Grothendieck tested the section-conjecture approach on Fermat curves and diagnosed the need for non-abelian levels, ahead of the published nilpotent-descent literature.
transcription_corrections: 'x_n est connu mod quotient de γ_n' should likely read 'x_n est connu mod opération de γ_n' (known up to the action of γ_n).

'à [?] similitude [?] donc de M̂[n]-conjugaison' is illegible in the transcription; the sense is '(the splitting known) up to M̂[n]-conjugation', with a phrase like 'il en est de même' / 'il s'ensuit'.
In (379), the first group is written nM̂ (= M̂[n]); the underbrace H^1(Γ_Q, Ẑ(1)) is labelled (Q^*)^.
The first line reads 'modulo M̂[n]-conjugaison impliquent celle des scindages correspondant à E_1' (E_1, not Σ_1).
